title: Access-code gate + clientId data-flow + day-themed floating items + Feb 14 Valentine celebration

requirements.summary: Replace Internet Identity login UX with an English access-code gate that unlocks the app only after entering the exact phrase.
acceptanceCriteria: On initial app open, the user sees a dedicated access screen (not the Internet Identity login screen).
The user cannot view the Seven Day Progress or Daily Experience screens until the correct code phrase is entered.
Entering a value that is not exactly "I love uhh deha" (after trimming leading/trailing whitespace) does not unlock the app and shows an error state/message.

After the correct code phrase is entered once, the app remains unlocked on refresh using local persistence (e.g., localStorage) until the user explicitly locks/logs out (if such a control is provided).
All user-facing text used for this gate is in English.

file_operations.description: Add a hook that manages the access-code gate state: validates input by trimming and comparing exactly to "I love uhh deha", persists an unlocked flag and the trimmed code phrase in localStorage, exposes unlock/lock helpers, and provides an error state/message for incorrect phrases.

Create a dedicated access screen UI (English-only copy) that prompts for the code phrase, shows an error state when incorrect, and calls the access-gate hook to unlock on success. Use existing shadcn/ui components for layout and inputs; Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Rework the root UI flow to remove the Internet Identity login screen from initial access: render the new AccessGateScreen until unlocked; once unlocked, render the existing Valentine Week UI. Add an explicit "Lock" control (in the header) that clears the unlocked state via the access-gate hook so refresh persistence behavior matches requirements.

requirements.summary: Remove Principal/Internet Identity dependency in frontend data-flow by using a locally generated, persisted clientId for all profile/progress reads and writes.
acceptanceCriteria: Frontend generates a stable clientId (stored locally) and uses it for all profile/progress reads and writes.
React Query keys for profile/progress are based on clientId (not identity principal).
Backend exposes corresponding endpoints that accept clientId (and any required access-code parameter) to get/save profile and to get/claim day progress.
The app can claim days and display progress without authenticating via Internet Identity.

file_operations.description: Add a hook to generate a stable clientId (e.g., crypto-random) on first run, persist it in localStorage, and return it for use across all React Query hooks and UI flows.

Update profile queries/mutations to use clientId-based backend capabilities (and include the stored access code phrase from the access-gate hook) instead of caller Principal. Ensure React Query keys include clientId and that queries are enabled only when actor is ready, app is unlocked, and clientId is available.

Update the Valentine progress query to be clientId-based (no identity principal). Change React Query keys to include clientId and ensure calls include the persisted access code phrase from the access-gate hook so the app works without Internet Identity.
Update the claim-day mutation to use clientId-based backend capabilities (and include the persisted access code phrase) and invalidate the clientId-based progress query key on success.

Adjust the profile setup flow to work without Internet Identity: keep the same modal UI, but ensure it saves/fetches profile using the clientId-based hooks and is shown based on unlocked + missing profile state (not authenticated principal).

Update App-level state wiring: remove identity-based gating and compute `showProfileSetup` from unlocked state + profile fetch state; ensure SevenDayProgress and DailyExperience render only after the access gate is unlocked.

Update frontend backend type declarations to reflect the new clientId + access-code-gated backend capabilities used by the modified hooks (no Principal-based methods for profile/progress in the primary app flow).

requirements.summary: Make floating/clickable items day-specific by swapping the floating asset per Valentine Week day while preserving pickup-line behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: On Rose Day, the floating items render with the existing rose/flower asset.
On Chocolate Day, the floating items render with a chocolate-themed asset.
On Teddy Day, the floating items render with a teddy-themed asset.
On Propose Day, Promise Day, Hug Day, and Kiss Day, the floating items each render with a distinct themed asset appropriate to that day.
Clicking/tapping the floating items continues to show pickup lines (existing behavior), regardless of which themed item is displayed.

file_operations.description: Add the generated asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/teddy-icon.dim_128x128.png so it can be used for Teddy Day floating items.
Add the generated asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/chocolate-icon.dim_128x128.png so it can be used for Chocolate Day floating items.
Add the generated asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/ring-icon.dim_128x128.png so it can be used for Propose Day floating items.
Add the generated asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/promise-icon.dim_128x128.png so it can be used for Promise Day floating items.
Add the generated asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/hug-icon.dim_128x128.png so it can be used for Hug Day floating items.
Add the generated asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/kiss-icon.dim_128x128.png so it can be used for Kiss Day floating items.

Update the floating-item renderer to select the correct image per `dayName` (Rose uses existing frontend/public/assets/generated/flower-icon.dim_128x128.png; Propose uses ring; Chocolate uses chocolate; Teddy uses teddy; Promise uses handshake/promise; Hug uses hug; Kiss uses kiss). Keep the click handler and pickup-line overlay logic unchanged.
If needed, adjust styling so new themed icons remain visually consistent (size, drop-shadow, hover/active) across all day-specific assets without changing the interaction model.

requirements.summary: Add a Feb 14 Valentine’s Day full-screen prompt and celebration that replaces normal 7-day content on that date.
acceptanceCriteria: When the current date is Feb 14, the Daily Experience area shows the Valentine prompt instead of the normal 7-day content.
The prompt text is exactly "Will you be my valentine?" and the two selectable options are exactly "Yes" and "Ofcourse".

After selecting either option, the app shows a full-screen celebration state containing the exact text "I love uhh deha" and a visible hearts effect (e.g., repeating hearts, animated hearts, or a heart-filled overlay).
All user-facing text used in this Valentine’s Day experience is in English.

file_operations.description: Add a small helper to detect whether the current date (using the same UTC approach as the week status) is Feb 14, so DailyExperience can switch to the Valentine’s Day prompt deterministically.

Create a component that renders the exact prompt "Will you be my valentine?" with exactly two options labeled "Yes" and "Ofcourse"; after selection, render a full-screen celebration overlay with the exact text "I love uhh deha" and a visible hearts effect (e.g., an overlay using frontend/public/assets/generated/heart-pattern.dim_1024x1024.png). Use existing shadcn/ui components where appropriate; Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Add styles/animation for the full-screen hearts effect/overlay used by the Feb 14 celebration state, keeping all user-facing text in English.

Wire the Feb 14 behavior: when the date helper indicates Feb 14, render ValentinesDayExperience in place of the normal Valentine Week content area (including replacing the flower field/claim button UI for that date). Ensure this switch happens before the normal week-active rendering logic.
